_comment: Workspace profile for the WhatsApp Local AI Assistant. Baileys linked-device bridge + local MCP server (stdio) for Claude Desktop/Code. All data stays local; Claude Pro subscription covers the AI cost with zero API billing. Token efficiency is the primary design constraint.
label: WhatsApp Local AI Assistant

metadata.description: Baileys WhatsApp bridge + MCP server that lets Claude Desktop/Code read, search, summarize, and (with approval) reply to WhatsApp messages — fully local, no API cost, token-efficient.

promptProfile:
wa-assistant conventions (this workspace):
- WhatsApp connection uses Baileys (@whiskeysockets/baileys) as a linked device — NO Playwright, NO Chrome, NO browser scraping.
- Session files live in auth_info/ (gitignored). On first run, print QR to terminal via qrcode-terminal. Persist session via useSingleFileAuthState or useMultiFileAuthState from Baileys.
- All DB access through src/store/db.ts singleton (better-sqlite3, synchronous). Never open a second DB connection.
- MCP server uses stdio transport (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk). Entry point: `node dist/index.js --mcp` for MCP mode, `node dist/index.js` for daemon mode.
- send_message tool MUST include a confirmation field in its response: the tool prepares the message but marks it 'pending' — Claude must call a confirm_send tool to actually dispatch it.
- Hard token budgets per Claude call: summarize ≤ 800 tokens out; QA ≤ 600 tokens out; reply suggestions ≤ 200 tokens out per option (3 options max).
- Every Claude interaction must log { operation, tokensIn, tokensOut } to ai_calls table.
- Run the local filter pipeline (src/filter/pipeline.ts) BEFORE any context is built for Claude — if it returns 'skip', no AI call is made.
- Strict TypeScript (strict:true), no `any`, explicit return types on all exports.
- Honor CLAUDE.md in the project root.
_foundation_note: FOUNDATION ALREADY IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED in the repo (commit b3876f6): WA-STORE (src/store/* — db singleton+migrations, messages with FTS5 search/dedup, contacts with VIP+rate-limit, chats, summaries+ai_calls ledger), WA-BRIDGE (src/bridge/client.ts — QR pairing, multi-file auth session, backoff reconnect), WA-SYNC (src/bridge/handler.ts — WAMessage normalize→store, NewMessageEvent emit), WA-MCP-CORE (src/mcp/server.ts — stdio scaffold + tool registry, src/index.ts dual --mcp/daemon mode + graceful shutdown with WAL flush), WA-MCP-SEARCH (src/mcp/tools/search.ts — search_messages tool), and list_chats (src/mcp/tools/list-chats.ts). tsc clean, 11/11 store runtime smoke tests pass. The remaining seed tasks below build ON this foundation — read the existing src/ files first; do NOT re-create the store/bridge/server scaffolding.

seed.title: send_message + confirm_send MCP tools: two-step send gate — send_message stages a pending message, confirm_send dispatches it via Baileys after Claude shows the user the draft
seed.notes: Build on the EXISTING src/mcp/server.ts (registerTool pattern — see registerListChats/registerSearch as the template) and src/bridge/client.ts getSock(). Create src/mcp/tools/send-message.ts (export registerSend) + src/mcp/tools/confirm-send.ts (export registerConfirmSend), and register both in buildServer(). send_message: params { chat_id, body } → returns { pending_id (use crypto.randomUUID), chat_name, body, warning: 'Review the message above and call confirm_send(pending_id) to dispatch.' }; store pending in a module-level Map<string, {chatId,body,expires}> with 5-min TTL. confirm_send: params { pending_id } → look up pending, call getSock()?.sendMessage(chatId, { text: body }); if sock is null → error 'bridge not connected'; remove from map; log via logAiCall('send',0,0). If pending_id missing/expired → error. NEVER auto-confirm.

seed.title: summarize_chat MCP tool: return an existing summary if fresh (< 10 new messages since last), otherwise generate a new one by sending only the delta + previous summary to Claude
seed.notes: Build on EXISTING store helpers: getLatestSummary/insertSummary/logAiCall (src/store/summaries.ts), getMessages/countMessagesSince (src/store/messages.ts). Create src/mcp/tools/summarize.ts (export registerSummarize) and register in buildServer(). params { chat_id, force_refresh?: boolean }. Logic: (1) latest = getLatestSummary(chat_id); (2) if latest && countMessagesSince(chat_id, latest.upToTs) <= 10 && !force_refresh → return cached summary text immediately (0 tokens, note 'cached'); (3) else load getMessages(chat_id, 100) since latest?.upToTs, build a compact transcript (each line '[HH:MM sender]: body'), prepend previous summary if present; (4) IMPORTANT — this MCP tool returns the assembled prompt/transcript as its text content for Claude (the connected Claude Desktop/Code session) to summarize in-context; the tool itself does NOT make a separate API call. After Claude returns a summary the user can persist it (a future persist_summary tool) — for now insertSummary on the assembled up_to_ts with tokens_used=0. Hard guidance in the returned text: 'Summarize in <=150 words, <=800 tokens.'

seed.title: Local routing pipeline: synchronous chain of heuristics that classifies each new incoming message as skip | notify | summarize | reply before any MCP tool is called by Claude
seed.notes: Create src/filter/rules.ts + src/filter/pipeline.ts exporting classify(event: NewMessageEvent): 'skip'|'notify'|'summarize'|'reply'. Use EXISTING helpers: getContact/aiCallsToday (src/store/contacts.ts), the chat.unreadCount on the event. Rules (in order, first match wins): (1) message.direction==='out' → 'skip'; (2) chat.isGroup && body has no @mention of this device's JID → 'skip'; (3) body.length < 5 → 'skip'; (4) contact?.isVip → 'reply'; (5) question pattern (body trimmed ends with '?', or matches /\b(מה|האם|כמה|מתי|איפה|who|what|when|where|how)\b/i) → 'notify'; (6) chat.unreadCount >= 5 → 'summarize'; (7) aiCallsToday(contactId) >= 10 → 'skip' (rate limit); (8) default 'skip'. INTEGRATION: in src/index.ts daemon mode, replace the existing `// TODO(WA-FILTER)` line inside onNewMessage with `const action = classify({message,chat}); console.error('[filter]', action, who)`. Add a focused test (node --test) for classify covering each rule.

seed.title: Claude Desktop config template + Windows startup: claude_config/claude_desktop_config.json template, Task Scheduler XML for auto-start on login, and a one-command setup script
seed.notes: The entry point already supports `--mcp` mode (src/index.ts). Create claude_config/claude_desktop_config.json: { mcpServers: { whatsapp: { command: 'node', args: ['<absolute-path>/dist/index.js', '--mcp'] } } }. claude_config/startup.xml: Windows Task Scheduler task that runs 'node <path>/dist/index.js' (daemon mode, NOT --mcp) at user logon, restart-on-failure. claude_config/setup.ps1: PowerShell that (a) npm run build, (b) merges the MCP config into %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json (preserve existing mcpServers), (c) registers the Task Scheduler task from startup.xml via schtasks. Document in comments: Claude Desktop must be restarted after the config change.

seed.title: Remaining read MCP tools: get_messages (chat_id + limit + before_ts cursor) and get_unread (all unprocessed inbound messages) — list_chats and search_messages already exist
seed.notes: list_chats (src/mcp/tools/list-chats.ts) and search_messages (src/mcp/tools/search.ts) are DONE — follow their exact pattern. Add src/mcp/tools/get-messages.ts (export registerGetMessages): params { chat_id, limit?, before_ts? } → use EXISTING getMessages(chatId, limit, beforeTs) from src/store/messages.ts; return compact rows { id, sender, body_preview: body.slice(0,100), ts }. Add src/mcp/tools/get-unread.ts (export registerGetUnread): add a store helper getUnprocessedInbound(limit) in messages.ts (SELECT * FROM messages WHERE ai_processed=0 AND direction='in' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT ?), join chat name via getChat; return compact rows grouped by chat. Register both in buildServer() (src/mcp/server.ts). Keep outputs token-lean — previews not full bodies.
